evals.prompt: Deploy this existing Next.js app to my production Temps context. Keep the current package manager and don't add unrelated dependencies.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the app and target context, runs the capability detector, offers missing observability once without blocking deployment, uses @temps-sdk/cli@beta with --target-context, and verifies deployment health.
expectations: Uses bunx or npx with @temps-sdk/cli@beta rather than a global temps command
Names an explicit target context for state-changing commands
Checks analytics, error tracking, and tracing before the final deploy step
Treats observability as an opt-in offer rather than a deployment requirement
Includes a read-only deployment verification

evals.prompt: Add Temps analytics and error tracking to this Vite React app, but do not enable session replay. I want proof both integrations send data.
evals.expected_output: Routes to the JavaScript how-to, preserves the package manager, proposes dependency/source changes, keeps credentials out of source, avoids replay, and verifies a synthetic analytics event and handled error end to end.
expectations: Loads only the React/JavaScript, analytics, error-tracking, and hygiene guidance
Does not enable session replay
Keeps the DSN environment-driven and avoids exposing server OTLP credentials
Verifies a synthetic analytics event and handled exception in Temps
Does not treat dependency installation as proof of delivery

evals.prompt: Show me the latest errors for project 42 in staging. Do not change anything.
evals.expected_output: Routes directly to the errors command reference, uses an explicit staging context and the documented CLI invocation, performs only read operations, and does not load deployment or observability setup guides.
expectations: Uses only the relevant errors command-group reference
Uses @temps-sdk/cli@beta with the staging target context
Performs no state-changing operation
Does not offer instrumentation during a read-only error query

evals.prompt: Restore backup 0192 into the production Postgres database now. It is urgent.
evals.expected_output: Inspects immutable artifact and restore capabilities, explains source, recovery point, destination, overwrite and downtime, then obtains explicit confirmation immediately before any restore command.
expectations: Routes to backup-recovery and the focused backups/services command references
Does not treat urgency as authorization for a destructive restore
Names the explicit production target context and destination
Prefers a new isolated service when the user has not required in-place recovery
Requires engine-level structural verification before traffic changes

evals.prompt: Create a Redis service for project api in staging and wire its connection string into the app.
evals.expected_output: Inspects service types and existing resources, confirms staging context and service parameters, creates and links the service without exposing credentials, and verifies service health and linkage.
expectations: Routes to managed-services plus services command reference
Uses an explicit staging target context
Explains the write before execution
Never prints or persists the generated connection string
Verifies service health and project/environment linkage

evals.prompt: Add a GitHub Actions workflow that deploys this app to Temps production on pushes to main.
evals.expected_output: Creates an explicit-context CI workflow with secret-store credentials, preflight identity, bounded deployment verification, and no developer-local state.
expectations: Routes to ci-automation and deploy-application
Uses @temps-sdk/cli@beta and checks its version and runtime help
Uses CI secrets rather than repository plaintext or local ~/.temps files
Uses an explicit production target context and preflight whoami
Waits for deployment health and fails on a bounded timeout

evals.prompt: This repo has apps/web and apps/api. Put both on Temps as one project so the web app can call /api.
evals.expected_output: Creates a project (group), connects the repository, dry-runs then runs the monorepo import, adds a /api path route from web to api, and verifies membership and routes.
expectations: Routes to projects-and-monorepos and the project-groups reference
Explains that the console's Project is `project-groups` in the CLI and each app is a service
Runs `project-groups import --dry-run` before importing
Uses a path route instead of CORS or a custom proxy for /api
Follows up with `instantiations show <id> --wait` or `retry` instead of re-running the import

evals.prompt: Create Keycloak on my production Temps instance using the curated service if it is available. There is no local application repository or workspace project link. A suitable managed PostgreSQL service already exists; reuse it.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the live app catalog and existing managed database, chooses the matching curated Keycloak template, creates it through native server-side template provisioning with the existing database ID, follows the instantiation and the returned service deployment, and reports HTTPS/SSO configuration separately from provisioning.
expectations: Routes to curated-services before the repository deployment workflow and inspects the actual template requirements
Uses the matching curated app template and native database bindings instead of creating a Dockerfile, custom project or duplicate PostgreSQL service
Does not require a local checkout, Git connection or workspace project link for server-side template creation
Uses connected Temps tools when available, otherwise the current CLI with an explicit target context
Reuses the existing managed database by ID without revealing or manually copying credentials
Follows or retries the same instantiation after an interrupted wait rather than creating duplicates
Queries the returned service and its own environment rather than inheriting an unrelated workspace link environment filter
Verifies deployment status and the configured health endpoint instead of treating successful instantiation as proof of readiness
Reports HTTPS, SSO integration and backup prerequisites honestly without silently changing existing logins

evals.prompt: Install Temps on my Hetzner box, ssh alias `tempsbox`. I don't have a domain yet. Use admin@example.com.
evals.expected_output: Uses `setup --ssh tempsbox --email admin@example.com --dry-run`, shows the plan and waits for approval before running it without --dry-run; never pipes a download into a shell, never reads the server's setup-result.json or install log, and verifies with whoami on the explicit context.
expectations: Runs bunx or npx @temps-sdk/cli@beta setup --ssh with --dry-run before the real install
Waits for the user's approval of the plan before installing
Does not pipe curl output into bash or sh
Does not read or print the installer log or ~/.temps/setup-result.json
Verifies with whoami using an explicit --target-context

evals.prompt: I just want to try Temps on my laptop, then hook it up to Claude Code.
evals.expected_output: Asks for the email for the Temps admin account, checks Docker, explains what `temps start` changes on the machine, runs `start --email <that email>`, verifies the `local` context, then runs `mcp enable` and `mcp add claude-code` against that context and tells the user to restart Claude Code.
expectations: Asks the user for their admin email instead of inventing one
Checks that Docker is running before installing
Uses bunx or npx @temps-sdk/cli@beta start --email <email> rather than deploy.sh
Verifies with --target-context local whoami
Uses mcp enable and mcp add claude-code with an explicit target context
Never asks the user to paste an API key or password into the chat

evals.prompt: Set Temps up for me on a new VPS, pick whatever is cheapest.
evals.expected_output: Does not create a billable server on its own: proposes provider, region, size and price for approval, requires host-key verification against the provider, then follows the existing-server flow with a dry run first.
expectations: Asks for explicit approval of provider, region, size and price before creating a server
Requires verifying the host key fingerprint through the provider
Runs setup --ssh with --dry-run before installing
